dossier.title: Database query performance audit
dossier.subtitle: Reviewed slow queries in production over the past month. Found three candidates for indexing.

blocks.text: We analyzed 50,000 slow queries (>500ms) from the production logs over 30 days. Three queries account for 65% of the slow query volume and all three lack covering indexes.
The three queries involve the users and orders tables. Index changes must be tested in staging first.

pages.title: Query details
pages.summary: The three slow queries and their index plans.

blocks.text: SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL. Runs 15,000 times per day, average 850ms.
Recommendation: Add index on (email, deleted_at). This is a covering index for the query condition.
Query 2: Recent orders for a user
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE user_id = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20. Runs 12,000 times per day, average 620ms.
Recommendation: Add index on (user_id, created_at). The sort order matches, so it covers both the filter and the sort.
Query 3: Search orders by date range
SELECT * FROM orders WHERE created_at BETWEEN ? AND ? AND status = ?. Runs 5,500 times per day, average 920ms.
Recommendation: Add index on (created_at, status). This covers both conditions.
